The Iraqi revolt of 1920 was an uprising against British rule in Iraq, from June to October 1920. Sunni and Shia Arabs, tribes and townspeople rose together, and Iraqis remember it as the Great Iraqi Revolution.

Britain had taken Iraq from the Ottomans in the First World War and was given a mandate by the League of Nations in 1920. Taxes, British officials and the denial of independence angered many. The revolt began on the Euphrates and was backed by Shia clerics of Najaf and Karbala.

British and Indian troops, with aircraft, crushed it; thousands of Iraqis and several hundred British and Indian soldiers died. Costs pushed Britain to set up a kingdom under Faisal I in 1921 and to rule through it. See also Iraq.
